## Decision record: what the projection face promises, and what its receipts look like

::: {.callout .callout-note}
**Decision.** CS-21 is a witness, not a specification: it freezes what the
exported `ms_embed()` face actually adjudicates over planted share matrices,
so future drift speaks immediately. It commits only machine-stable facts: the
error CLASS always, and the message CLAUSES verbatim -- every one of them.
The face walks a six-step gate ladder (input, method, transform, seed, the
cluster bound, the kmeans sample-axis window) and returns a plain
`data.frame` of projection coordinates, so the accepted render commits the
container's discrete identity -- class, field names, per-column classes,
shape, the integer cluster vector, an all-finite glyph, the zero-total sample
index and the digit-scrubbed sample head -- and never a float payload: the
coordinates' last bits are ill-conditioned and would not reproduce across
platforms. Two clauses interpolate measured quantities, so the lane scrubs
every digit to `#` before freezing bytes; and the `match.arg` failures speak
apostrophe-free heads because the lane strips quote glyphs first. One
finding is load-bearing: the two `match.arg` refusals ride the BASE class
`simpleError`, not `msuiter_error_input` -- the shipped face's option-gate
abort is a plain R error, and the witness freezes that contract as shipped.
Under the D11 cross-platform posture every committed arm is integer, label,
logical, class or clause bytes. The lane also reproduced, live, the face's
gate ORDER: input outranks method, method outranks transform, transform
outranks seed, seed outranks the cluster bound, and the bound outranks the
sample-axis window.
:::

### The face

`ms_embed(exposures, method = c("umap", "kmeans"), transform = c("share",
"none"), seed = 1, clusters = 3L)` is the exported face (`R/ms-embed.R:43`)
that projects samples into a two-dimensional embedding space for
visualization. It validates the exposure matrix, resolves both option
gates through `match.arg`, checks the seed, names the samples, applies the
share transform, and for `kmeans` bounds the cluster count by the signature
count, refuses degenerate windows, and runs `stats::kmeans` with ten restarts
before relabelling clusters by the first centre coordinate. The face measures
278 lines. CS-21 fires 40 observation arms at it: 12 law arms, 8 acceptance
specs, 12 precedence discriminators, 8 degenerate rows (4 pairs), 16 scalars.
The committed lane replays every arm live: the law file adjudicates 275
expectations across 10 units (0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped, 0 warnings) and
the runner rails every row against the frozen block before any witness byte
is written.

### The ladder, the scrub, and why the census splits three ways

The law ladder walks the six gates in the order the face ships them. **The
input gate** refuses anything that is not a numeric k x n matrix or an
`MsSignature` -- "exposures must be a numeric k x n matrix (or an
MsSignature)" -- naming the received class and the fit/refit remedy. **The
option gates** run `match.arg` on `method` and `transform`, and here the
witness records a base-class contract: the abort is `simpleError`, not the
package's `msuiter_error_input`. The committed clauses are apostrophe-free
("arg should be one of umap, kmeans", "arg should be one of share, none")
because `.cs21_quote` drops every quote glyph before bytes freeze. **The
seed gate** refuses negative, missing and non-finite seeds with a clause
that interpolates the received value, so the lane digit-scrubs it to
"received: #" -- the frozen text stays portable across platforms while the
actual bound is sealed separately as scalars. **The cluster bound** refuses
centres outside `[1, n signatures]`, again with an interpolated clause; **the
sample-axis window** refuses the counts `stats::kmeans` itself cannot abide
(one centre, or one centre per sample). The 40-arm class census
(`data.frame=10`, `msuiter_error_input=22`, `simpleError=8`) is recomputed
from the frozen vectors inside the law file -- a silent class shift reddens
the lane, not the reader.

### The laws the face demonstrates

- **The input law.** A bare string and a bare list both refuse at the first
  gate as `msuiter_error_input`, before any option is read.
- **The seed law.** A length-two vector, a negative seed, `NA` and `Inf` all
  refuse as `msuiter_error_input` with the digit-scrubbed clause; the seed
  argument must be a single non-negative finite number.
- **The method and transform laws.** A bogus `method` and a bogus
  `transform` each refuse through their own `match.arg` gate as
  `simpleError`, with apostrophe-free option lists.
- **The cluster bound law.** Zero centres and eight centres on a
  five-signature plant both refuse -- the bound is signed, not just a floor.
- **The window law.** One cluster on nine samples refuses, because
  `stats::kmeans` refuses one centre and centre-per-sample counts alike.
- **Precedence.** Twelve discriminators, each with its fires anchor pinned
  PRESENT and its anti anchor pinned ABSENT in the same live message:
  input > method > transform > seed > cluster-bound > cluster-window.
- **The acceptance specs.** Seven arms accept and commit the full discrete
  render -- `data.frame|sample,embed_1,embed_2,cluster|9x4|
  character,numeric,numeric,integer|<cluster vector>|1|<zero-total index>|
  <scrubbed head>`. Two centres re-shade the same nine samples into a
  2-then-1 ladder; five centres split the first block again; `transform =
  "none"`, the default seed and the argument order all fold onto the design
  bytes; the nameless plant moves only the scrubbed sample head, which
  speaks a `sample#` placeholder instead of a planted label. The eighth arm
  is the bound's own contrast: eight centres ride past the signature count
  and the face refuses with the scrubbed clusters-bound clause -- the same
  bytes the law ladder records.
- **The boundary pairs.** Unlike the single-axis ladders of the earlier
  witnesses, these pairs contrast accept against reject (the planted accept
  against the input-gate refusal), reject against reject across two distinct
  cluster gates (six centres ride past the signature bound while the square
  six-by-six plant passes the bound and dies at the sample-axis window),
  accept against accept across the all-zero share guard (the zero-total
  sample re-shades the cluster ladder and its own row becomes the committed
  zero-total index), and the two `match.arg` heads from adjacent rungs.

### The receipts

| receipt | committed bytes |
|---|---|
| `cs21_laws.tsv` | 12 arms: class split `msuiter_error_input` (10) and `simpleError` (2, the `match.arg` pair), every clause verbatim, every mode `reject` |
| `cs21_specs.tsv` | 8 arms: 7 accepted renders (class `data.frame` plus the eight discrete fields) and the bound's own contrast refusing with the clusters-bound clause |
| `cs21_precedence.tsv` | 12 discriminators, each with its fires anchor PRESENT and its anti anchor ABSENT in the live message |
| `cs21_degenerates.tsv` | 4 boundary pairs (8 rows): accept/reject across the input gate, reject/reject across two distinct cluster gates, accept/accept across the all-zero share guard, and the two `match.arg` heads -- hi and lo committed side by side |
| `cs21_scalars.tsv` | 16 keys: the three class scalars (input gate, `match.arg`, accepted container), the accepted shape (`clusters-chosen`, `rows`, `cols`, `names`, `classes`), the cluster vector, the scrubbed sample head, the all-finite glyph, the zero-total pair, and both RNG-purity rails |

All five witnesses byte-reproduce on consecutive runner invocations (twice
witnessed at build time), the plant and spec corpora hash identically under
BOTH governed SHA-256 kernels (`.ms_fit_sha256` and digest), the RNG-purity
rails read `FALSE` before and after -- a caller who never seeded holds no
stream afterwards -- and the lane never calls the benchmark driver, the
declined calibration family, the registry face or any validator internal
(banned words, grepped over the runner source).

### What the lane deliberately leaves unwitnessed

No arm drives the umap kernel. The lane adjudicates the umap-facing gates
(the `method` option law, the seed law on a `umap` call), but the kernel's
projection bytes are platform-conditioned and -- under the D11 posture that
governs this lane -- would not be committable as frozen payloads anyway.
The committed record therefore covers the face's refusal ladder, the kmeans
acceptance path and the RNG contract; the umap kernel's numeric behavior
stays outside the frozen ledger by design, not by omission.

### The single-source build, and the audit that became the minter

Both hosts -- law file and runner -- carry one byte-identical frozen block and
one byte-identical shared code block, each injected from a single source
between BEGIN/END markers; the splice rail demands the exact marker counts and
compares the two regions across the files byte for byte. The minter IS the
audit: every one of the 40 roster arms is re-fired LIVE through the face
against the audited probe ledger; each of the 12 precedence arms carries an
explicit FIRES/ANTI pair asserted order-invariantly; every scalar is
re-fireable and re-fired -- including the two RNG-rail scalars, which ride
their own frozen expressions now that the refire table covers all sixteen
keys. The committed clause bytes in this page are read from the committed
witnesses, never re-typed from plan.

### What the lane-building itself caught (the honest section)

The live replay killed four would-be-innocent readings before one witness
byte was trusted. First, the minter's precedence assertions died on the
`match.arg` clauses: the quote-stripping pass removes apostrophes too, so
the frozen clause is "arg should be one of umap, kmeans" -- the authored
anchor had quoted option names and matched nothing. Second, a DEGEN
assertion compared `vapply()` output over a NAMED arm vector with
`identical()`, which is attribute-strict: the comparison had to be
`unname()`d or every pair row read as drift. Third, the law file's scalar
unit initially re-fired the two RNG keys through `.cs21_scalval()`, whose
switch deliberately has no branch for them -- the mint had moved the RNG
rail INTO the refire table, so the unit now re-fires those two keys through
their own frozen expressions and the fourteen render keys through the shared
probe. Fourth, the byte-identity verifier itself dropped the shared block's
last line: the two-line SHARED-END marker anchors at its first line, so the
core slice had to stop one line earlier. All four findings were caught by
the lane's own rails, before any witness byte was committed.

### Provenance

The frozen block and the shared code block in both hosts are minted
mechanically from the audited probe ledger (audit green: 40 arms byte-exact
on live re-fire, 8 degen rows, 12/12 fires-and-anti anchors, 16 scalars
re-fired); neither is ever hand-edited in place. The plants' canonical texts
hash to the committed dual-kernel checksums
(`plant_sha256=4b31bef1fa68077c969d9349b0ba6c5475b276df7dc16240ffcc434f7cb5a9db`,
`spec_sha256=d29e4f13413ae480127f699355297c1a9544f84e7a2a51114e08db05ce88b2f2`);
reifying the lane reproduces every witness byte for byte (witness sha256
`cs21_laws=41543db9...`, `cs21_specs=79ab5b2f...`,
`cs21_precedence=b288fb20...`, `cs21_degenerates=c88454f2...`,
`cs21_scalars=19eb6b16...`). Differentiation from CS-20 (the rank-selection
face): CS-20 adjudicated a three-LAYER arbitration returning a plain list
with a documented placeholder column; CS-21 adjudicates a visualization
gate-ladder whose accepted render is a `data.frame` of coordinates -- the
first witness in the series whose refusal split includes a BASE-class
`simpleError` contract, the first whose interpolation forces digit-scrubbed
refusal clauses, and the first whose boundary pairs contrast accept against
accept on both sides of a guard.

### Gate forensics

The scenarios leg for this lane (the twenty-first) was render-verified before
the full local burn. The T0 seal moved 629 -> 630 with the generator's refusal
witnessed verbatim (the DEFECT line naming 630 against the sealed 629, run
against the freshly re-weighted shard roster) before the deliberate re-seal,
per the budget law; the reified manifest carries the new law file on the T0
tier, byte-deterministic on re-mint.
